issue_context.title: When converting to SVG the "fill-opacity: 1" attribute should not be added if the "fill" attribute is missing
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
 [http://www.mediafire.com/file/jz26jy0zz326pw3/hypothermia-prevention-and-management-in-adults-having-surgery-update+Dec2016.pdf](http://www.mediafire.com/file/jz26jy0zz326pw3/hypothermia-prevention-and-management-in-adults-having-surgery-update+Dec2016.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Google Chrome 73.0.3683.103 (Official Build) (64-bit)
- Operating system and its version: Ubuntu 18.04
- PDF.js version: "pdfjs-dist": "~2.0.943"
- Is a browser extension: No

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Upload and convert the pdf file to SVG.

What is the expected behavior?
Create the svg file without the "fill-opacity: 1" attribute since the "fill" attribute is missing.

What went wrong? (add screenshot)
The pages from 2 to the last have the "fill-opacity: 1" attribute, but do not have the "fill" attribute, so the browser paints all these pages into black color by default: [https://www.dropbox.com/s/fgrcdr5573cwf81/Screen%20Shot%202019-05-02%20at%2015.37.21.png?dl=0](https://www.dropbox.com/s/fgrcdr5573cwf81/Screen%20Shot%202019-05-02%20at%2015.37.21.png?dl=0)

Link to a viewer (if hosted on a site other than mozilla.github.io/pdf.js or as Firefox/Chrome extension): None
comments:
This issue is caused by the fact that tiling patterns have not been implemented in the SVG back-end. The background of the pages contains a tiling pattern that fills the whole page with white and draws the horizontal header and footer lines. 

https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/fef86cc3e327f0554136482fee901b52909fa37a/src/display/svg.js#L983-L989

Because `null` is returned, `<path>` elements won't have any `fill` attribute and the default value `fill="black"` makes the pages black.

review_comments: This line appears to break the PDF file from #10487, which also uses tiling patterns. Could you check why that happens?

The #10487 PDF uses the TilingPattern on the first page only.
Before implementing TilingPattern, paths that should be drawn in red were black with `fill=""`.
Looking at the output of this PR implementation, the rendering of `<svg:pattern>` using `<svg:g clip-path="...">` is broken.
I can infer from this that there might be a mistake in the implementation associated with clip, but I don't know exactly what is wrong.

I have been thinking about this some more and I think it's best to leave fixing this for a follow-up. The PDF file already wasn't rendering correctly and there is an open issue for it. Given that this patch improves the other PDF files, I don't see this as a blocker for landing this.
